handback.t:
I built the `hebbian_mesh` routing option for howler. It's off by default, and following your mid-task instruction it is now a thin adapter over the Rust `neural-mesh` CLI. On the simulated workload it beats howler's existing selection by +6.5 points success rate (95% CI excludes zero). It does not beat a plain Thompson-sampling bandit overall.

Nothing is committed; I stayed on branch `neural-mesh-router`. I installed nothing globally, only into a repo-local `.venv/` (already gitignored). I did not touch the MCP setup, skills or agents. The uncommitted `.claude/*` and `.mcp.json` changes in the tree were there before I started, and I left them alone.

**Integration points**
- **Howler never routed tasks before.** In `evolution/loop.py:~140` (`EvolutionLoop.step`) every agent runs every task. The only "which agent" choice is `PerformanceNoveltySelector` (`selection/criterion.py:30`), which keeps survivors by combined performance + novelty score, and `AgentPool.top_k` (`agents/pool.py:34`), which picks the best agent.
- **Outcomes are recorded** in the same loop (`TaskResult.score`, written as an `EvolutionaryTrace`), and in `LocalRunner.submit_experience` (`local_runner.py:~623`) for outside task results.
- **Hive-mind** (`hivemind/coordinator.py`) only stores memory and consensus, so there was nothing to hook there.
- **Where I wired in:**
  - `EvolutionLoop.__init__`: a router is built only when the flag is on.
  - The evaluation loop: each agent's task score is sent to the CLI.
  - New `EvolutionLoop.route_task` and `record_outcome` methods.
  - `LocalRunner`: the run keeps its router, there is a new `route_task`, and `submit_experience` sends the score back.

**Files**
- **Added:**
  - `packages/howler-agents-core/src/howler_agents/routing/__init__.py`
  - `packages/howler-agents-core/src/howler_agents/routing/router.py`: the CLI adapter.
  - `packages/howler-agents-core/tests/test_routing.py`: 13 tests.
  - `packages/howler-agents-core/tests/_fake_neural_mesh.py`: a stand-in CLI used only by tests.
  - `packages/howler-agents-core/benchmarks/routing_ab.py`
- **Modified:** `config.py` (new `RoutingConfig`, default `strategy="default"`), `evolution/loop.py`, `local_runner.py`.
- **Removed:** my first pure-Python version of the algorithm, so the Rust crate is the single source of truth.

**How to enable**
- In code: `HowlerConfig(routing=RoutingConfig(strategy="hebbian_mesh", binary=r"C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\target\release\neural-mesh.exe", team_size=1))`.
- Or set the env variable `HOWLER_NEURAL_MESH_BIN` instead of `binary`.
- Or call `LocalRunner.configure(routing_strategy="hebbian_mesh")`.
- Each CLI call has a 2 s timeout. Any failure (missing binary, timeout, error, bad JSON) falls back to `pool.top_k`. After 3 failures in a row the router switches itself off for the rest of the run.

**Tests**
- **Before:** 173 passed (CLAUDE.md's "52" is out of date).
- **After:** 186 passed (173 existing + 13 new). The 13 new tests cover:
  - Adapter: routing, feedback, error/garbage/timeout fallback, self-disable, missing binary.
  - Flag off: no router is built and `route_task` returns exactly `top_k`.
  - Flag on: evaluation scores reach the CLI; a broken CLI falls back.
  - Real binary: converges to the best agent, re-adapts after a skill drift, a failure lowers the weight, an unhealthy node is benched and skipped.
- **One flaky existing test:** `test_experience_pool_scales_sublinearly` failed once in a run made while the benchmark was loading the machine, and it fails when run alone. It is a wall-clock timing check on experience-pool code I didn't change, and it passes in the clean full run.

**A/B results** (30 seeds, paired per-seed differences, mean [95% t-CI], wins out of 30)

The simulated world has 6 task types and 8 agents with hidden skills, noise and misleading keywords, a mid-run skill drift, a stretch where one agent always fails, and team tasks with hidden helpful pairs. All strategies get the same warm-up data. The best possible solo-agent success rate is 0.851.

| Strategy | Overall success | Late (after drift) | Team tasks |
|---|---|---|---|
| howler default (performance + novelty, α 0.5) | 0.563 | 0.565 | 0.630 |
| howler performance only (α 1.0) | 0.588 | 0.591 | 0.671 |
| Thompson sampling (reference bandit) | 0.633 | 0.678 | 0.697 |
| hebbian_mesh (Rust CLI) | 0.628 | 0.629 | 0.726 |

hebbian_mesh minus each baseline:

| Baseline | Overall | Late | Failure window | Team |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| howler default | +0.065 [+0.036, +0.094], 22/30 | +0.064 [+0.031, +0.096] | +0.046 [+0.008, +0.084] | +0.096 [+0.055, +0.137] |
| howler performance only | +0.040 [+0.014, +0.066], 21/30 | +0.038 [+0.008, +0.068] | +0.023 (not significant) | +0.055 [+0.010, +0.100] |
| Thompson sampling | −0.006 [−0.019, +0.007], 13/30 | −0.049 [−0.070, −0.029] | +0.032 [+0.006, +0.058] | +0.029 [+0.007, +0.051] |

**Verdict:** On this simulation, `hebbian_mesh` clearly beats howler's existing selection on every measure. Most of that gain is because howler's score ignores task type, so it backs one generalist for everything. Against Thompson sampling it is a wash overall: better on team tasks and while an agent is failing, but significantly worse after the drift. The CLI uses its own built-in default settings here; nothing was tuned.

With my removed Python version tuned on seeds 1–8 I measured 0.687 overall and +0.054 over Thompson. That suggests the Rust defaults (eta 0.5, epsilon 0.02, decay 0.01) are too aggressive, but the CLI exposes no flags to set them.

**Things to know**
- The CLI has no way to copy a parent's weights to a child or drop dead agents, so new children start cold and old ids stay in the state file.
- Feedback sent through `submit_experience` only has the description to go on, so its features come from description keywords. They only line up with `route_task` if you pass the same kind of task dict to both.
- Each CLI call takes about 31 ms, about 88 s per seed in the benchmark. The benchmark runs seeds in parallel with `--jobs`. To reproduce: `.venv/Scripts/python packages/howler-agents-core/benchmarks/routing_ab.py --seeds 30 --bin <exe> --jobs 8`.

**Decision for you:** whether to add hyperparameter flags to the Rust CLI, re-tune on seeds 1–8 and re-run seeds 1–30. The cost is CLI work on the other agent's side. My Python numbers suggest it would close or reverse the gap to Thompson sampling, but I can't confirm that with the CLI as it is.
